row_counting_rule: count_rows.py is the executable form of this count; run it, do not trust the numbers beside it. RULE: a row is a line whose stripped form starts with '|', excluding lines inside ``` fences (those are examples of table syntax, not rows of this audit) and excluding GFM separator lines '|---|---|' (punctuation). Header rows ARE counted -- a choice, not a discovery: it is the rule under which two of the four original numbers reproduce, so it changes the fewest recorded figures. data_rows (header excluded, one per table) is recorded alongside for the other convention. The point is that the convention is written down, not which won.
